pr_body:
Fixes: #11330

Previously, the output of ADBCConnectionGetObjects did not output results in the [schema expected](https://github.com/apache/arrow-adbc/blob/ff866d9e2a696accbff3de3157eff70b3509fa79/adbc.h#L1468) by ADBC.

This fix ensures that the proper schema is used for GetObjects at all search depths and with any filter patterns.

Additionally:
- `depth='catalog'` is now implemented
- `table_type` is now included in results but still not valid for filtering (not implemented in upstream api)
- Table constraints are now included in the results (see limitations)

Limitations:
- The official GetObjects result schema specifies certain fields to be `not null`. The nullability is technically part of the schema, so it must be specified to have an exact schema match. In practice this would likely require defining the schema explicitly rather than deriving it from the query result to get it exact. That may be a better approach but at least for this implementation the response should be compatible with what most consumers would be expecting.
- Table constraints `names` and `types` are added to the response, but the current `information_schema` tables only contain `column` information for certain constraint types. For consistency across all constraint types, I've left the constraint-column fields as NULL.

issue_context.title: ADBC driver ConnectionGetObjects method does not return the standard schema
issue_context.body:
### What happens?

ADBC standardizes schemas for a number of the methods it exposes, including `ConnectionGetObjects`. The current `ConnectionGetObjects` implementation returns arrow records with a slightly different schema, with the effect that applications relying on the standard schema may break after calling the method.

The structure is defined in a comment in [adbc.h](https://github.com/apache/arrow-adbc/blob/ff866d9e2a696accbff3de3157eff70b3509fa79/adbc.h#L1468) and there is a [C++ helper](https://github.com/apache/arrow-adbc/blob/ff866d9e2a696accbff3de3157eff70b3509fa79/c/driver/common/utils.c#L442) specifying the schema as well.

The main issue is that DuckDB returns `db_schema_name`, `db_schema_tables` at the top-level, but they should actually be nested within a struct below `catalog_name` and `catalog_db_schemas`. There are also fields missing from the schema much more deeply nested such as xdbc and constraint info, but those fields can be reasonably set to null if they cannot be determined.

I have confirmed in the current HEAD of the source code that the described behavior is still the case.

### To Reproduce

```python
import adbc_driver_duckdb
with adbc_driver_duckdb.dbapi.connect() as conn:
    objects = conn.adbc_get_objects(depth="all").read_all()
print(objects.schema)

db_schema_name: string
db_schema_tables: list<l: struct<table_name: string, table_columns: list<l: struct<column_name: string, ordinal_position: int32, remarks: string>>>>
  child 0, l: struct<table_name: string, table_columns: list<l: struct<column_name: string, ordinal_position: int32, remarks: string>>>
      child 0, table_name: string
      child 1, table_columns: list<l: struct<column_name: string, ordinal_position: int32, remarks: string>>
          child 0, l: struct<column_name: string, ordinal_position: int32, remarks: string>
              child 0, column_name: string
              child 1, ordinal_position: int32
              child 2, remarks: string
```

compare to...

comments:
I played around with this a little bit. This query should return the correct structure for maximum object depth:
```sql
select
    table_catalog catalog_name,
    LIST(table_schema_list) catalog_db_schemas,
from (
    select
        table_catalog,
        {
            db_schema_name: table_schema,
            db_schema_tables: LIST(table_list),
        } table_schema_list
    from (
        select
            table_catalog,
            table_schema,
            {
                table_name: table_name,
                table_type: NULL::VARCHAR,
                table_columns: LIST(column_list),
                table_constraints: LIST(constraint_list),
            } table_list
        from (
            select
                table_catalog,
                table_schema,
                table_name,
                {
                    column_name: column_name,
                    ordinal_position: ordinal_position,
                    remarks : '',
                    xdbc_data_type: NULL::SMALLINT,
                    xdbc_type_name: NULL::VARCHAR,
                    xdbc_column_size: NULL::INTEGER,
                    xdbc_decimal_digits: NULL::SMALLINT,
                    xdbc_num_prec_radix: NULL::SMALLINT,
                    xdbc_nullable: NULL::SMALLINT,
                    xdbc_column_def: NULL::VARCHAR,
                    xdbc_sql_data_type: NULL::SMALLINT,
                    xdbc_datetime_sub: NULL::SMALLINT,
                    xdbc_char_octet_length: NULL::INTEGER,
                    xdbc_is_nullable: NULL::VARCHAR,
                    xdbc_scope_catalog: NULL::VARCHAR,
                    xdbc_scope_schema: NULL::VARCHAR,
                    xdbc_scope_table: NULL::VARCHAR,
                    xdbc_is_autoincrement: NULL::BOOLEAN,
                    xdbc_is_generatedcolumn: NULL::BOOLEAN,
                } column_list,
                {
                    constraint_name: NULL::VARCHAR,
                    constraint_type: NULL::VARCHAR,
                    constraint_column_names: NULL::VARCHAR[],
                    constraint_column_usage: NULL::STRUCT(fk_catalog VARCHAR, fk_db_schema VARCHAR, fk_table VARCHAR, fk_column_name VARCHAR)[],
                } constraint_list,
            from information_schema.columns
        ) group by table_catalog, table_schema, table_name
    ) group by table_catalog, table_schema
) group by table_catalog
```

For other object depths, the same schema should be used but excluded fields should be empty/null. Note that the result of this query still does not match the expected schema _exactly_. The structure of all fields is correct but certain fields should explicitly not be nullable (see which ones in the spec). This would likely involve defining/manipulating the result schema beyond what the implicit conversion of query results to arrow produces.

Note that `table_type` is `NULL`. The field is available in `information_schema.tables` but not in `information_schema.columns`. It didn't feel worth it to join the two for this one field.

Also note that I nulled out most of the xdbc and constraint info. This is fine from a compatibility perspective, but duckdb does have some of this info. I played around with joining to the constraint tables in the information_schema but wasn't able to produce the results I expected, particularly with composite primary keys. This is fine to leave out for now if it complicates things.

review_comments: Are these a restriction in the ADBC spec?

It's not specified in the spec, but neither the sqlite nor postgres drivers currently include system tables. This is a good point, because I think clarity about this is currently missing from the spec. I'm going ask on the arrow mailing list about this.

Thanks for the approval @pdet. The only part that remains is this catalog/schema filter. I've confirmed that the spec does not require system tables to be excluded. I can remove the filter and update the tests.
